title: Choose the visual world for WCI '27
question: The roll landed on Pit Trade, festival-scale FTC button and sticker culture. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Pit Trade
options.lineage: FTC pit trading: pin-back team buttons, die-cut vinyl stickers, lanyard credentials, scaled up to festival size
options.thesis: The whole site is the stuff teams trade in the pits: every team, date, and link is a button or sticker slapped onto the WCI sunset.
materials: flat concentric sunset arcs from the logo
options.viewport: A huge stacked WEST COAST INVITATIONAL '27 over the logo's sunset arcs, the countdown on a giant coral button, robot and host photos as pin-back buttons, the Apply action as a die-cut sticker.
options.risk: Too many stickers and it turns into clutter; logistics pages have to stay calm.

raised.raise: Full color commitment: sunset orange and coral own whole regions on every screen, not just accents.
Logistics text stays calm and plain; the stickers live around the edges, never on top of the info.
Team Info becomes one numbered path: Apply, Accepted, Pay, Packet, Load-in, Compete.
Each logistics section leads with one highlighted must-know line.
Venue, ER, parking, and food trucks share one annotated map instead of scattered address blocks.

options.label: Festival Lineup Poster
options.lineage: summer music-festival lineup posters with tiered billing
options.thesis: WCI billed like a festival: teams as the lineup, tiered by type size, on a banded sunset.
options.viewport: A centered lineup: name and date up top, team numbers billed in shrinking tiers, the event extras as the bottom row.
options.risk: Familiar: most festival-themed sites land here, and it needs a team list that won't exist until spring.

options.label: Surf Mag Layout Desk
options.thesis: WCI as a surf-culture magazine spread: type crashing through black-and-white event photos.
options.viewport: A grayscale photo of the emcee, condensed type overprinted across it, one coral spot color.
options.case: West Coast and loud, so it holds on audience feel, but reading order is earned rather than given, and that hurts the logistics pages teams rely on.
options.risk: Hard to read on a phone in a loud gym.

options.label: Treasure Map
options.viewport: A parchment map of the event.
options.risk: Teams don't want to solve their schedule.
options.kept: Venue and travel live on one annotated map.

options.label: Hand-Drawn Zine
options.thesis: A friend sketching the format on a napkin.
options.case: Clear, but far from big-festival scale.
options.kept: One highlighted must-know line per section.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.thesis: Sections strung along a perforated rail.
options.risk: An editing-room metaphor nobody here shares.
options.case: No link to teams or festivals.

options.label: Orizuru Sequence
options.risk: Quiet and foreign to the audience.
options.kept: One strict numbered sequence for the team journey.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud
options.kept: Reading areas stay calm while color lives at the edges.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean robotics-event site: hero photo, date, apply button, info cards.
canonCard.viewport: Full-bleed field photo, name and date, Apply and Schedule buttons, a row of feature cards below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other FTC event site; not festival.
